findings.title: Copied syntax-repair command permits shell injection through an unquoted path
findings.where: src/components/ConfigHygiene.tsx:275 constructs `python3 -m json.tool` by directly appending `syntaxFinding.sourcePath` or `health.filePath`; lines 335 and 340-342 advertise and copy that string as a command.
findings.what: A path containing shell metacharacters, command substitution, or whitespace is inserted verbatim into a command intended for execution. Running the copied command can execute attacker-chosen shell syntax or target a different file. React escaping does not protect clipboard command text.
findings.fix: Format the path as one shell-safe argument before constructing the command. Preserve `~/` semantics by explicitly mapping it to a quoted `$HOME` prefix, and single-quote/escape all remaining path text; do not concatenate a raw path into shell source.
findings.acceptance: Add a component test whose syntax-finding source path contains spaces, a single quote, semicolon, and command-substitution characters; copy the command and verify a shell parser sees exactly `python3`, `-m`, `json.tool`, and the original path as four arguments, with no additional command.
findings.verifyNote: Adversarially re-read src/components/ConfigHygiene.tsx:270-347 and the copy-command tests at src/components/ConfigHygiene.test.ts:296-340 in baseline c8b98a29508b5eb7725c75a7e2a41dfa94c1feba. The production interpolation remains unquoted; existing tests cover only metacharacter-free `~/.claude/...` paths and do not invalidate the injection case.

findings.title: Settings repair snippet is not copy-paste-safe for valid filesystem paths
findings.where: src/components/ConfigHygiene.tsx:275 builds the repair snippet without argument quoting, and lines 335 and 340-342 present it as a runnable, copyable fix.
findings.what: Even without malicious input, a valid settings path containing spaces, quotes, glob characters, or other shell-significant characters is split or transformed by the shell, so the validated repair instruction can fail or inspect the wrong artifact.
findings.fix: Centralize shell-argument serialization and construct the snippet from a safely quoted path, with an explicit safe expansion for a leading `~/`.
findings.acceptance: Parameterized tests copy repair commands for ordinary, spaced, quoted, glob-containing, and leading-tilde paths, then verify each command resolves to the exact original input path as one json.tool argument.
findings.verifyNote: The second pass re-read the command construction and both baseline copy assertions. The assertions establish the copied output but exercise only simple paths; no quoting or escaping occurs before the snippet reaches CopyButton, so the copy-paste failure survives verification.
